question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2x},\, & x\ge 0 \\ 0,\, & x<0\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<0 \\ h(x),\, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $x\ge 0,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & =-{e}^{-2t}{|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-{e}^{-2x}+1 \\  & =1-{e}^{-2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0, \\ 1-{e}^{-2x}, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$
